instances.fault_description: H3 Plot.nudge adds the scaled offset to the unexploded bounds when it should subtract it. The repository convention (H2 PlotUtilities.offset = point1 - point2, an inward vector from the exploded ring back to the unexploded ring) is correct. Because nudge adds that inward vector, the section moves toward the pie centre: x = 112.5 instead of 87.5. This is a sign or direction convention mismatch written as the natural opposite binary operator.

All 5 Sonnet runs and 4 of 5 Opus runs ranked offset first and argued it 'should be point2 - point1'.

instances.fault_description: H3 ExtraFieldUtils.widen receives the already-unsigned byte value (0..255) from H2 magnitudeOf. It splits that value into low = m & 0x7f and top = m - low, then recombines them as low - top, which re-signs the value, instead of low + top (identity). As a result, bytes with the top bit set contribute -128..-1 and the UTF-8 header checksum is -51 instead of 461.
instances.local_cue_gold_note: Both hops carry the same split/recombine form 'low - top' (revision 2 removed the canonical 'raw & 0xff' at H2), so the two-hop packet does not show which hop should transform. There is only a weak lexical hint: a method named 'widen' that changes the value.
instances.local_cue_decoy_note: The correct H2 magnitudeOf uses a non-idiomatic but valid unsigned conversion (low - top with a negative top), textually identical to the gold line.

instances.fault_description: H3 CharSetUtils.smalls folds a character pair only when all case forms agree (agreement == 2). The repository convention is any form (agreement > 0), as used by StringUtils.foldEquals. As a result, LONG S vs 's' and KELVIN vs 'K' fail to match ignoring case on the CharSequence path, and equalsIgnoreCase(StringBuilder, String) returns false while equalsIgnoreCase(String, String) returns true.
instances.local_cue_gold_note: Requiring full agreement of the case forms is a coherent alternative convention given akin's neutral javadoc, and V15/V16 passed. However, the trigger test's comment states that pairs whose upper forms agree and lower forms differ, or the reverse, compare equal. That makes the strict check convictable from the test.
instances.local_cue_decoy_note: The correct H2 akin returns an agreement count (upper + lower, 0..2). This is mildly unusual but not wrong. In the miss, the agent traced akin returning 1 and still ranked it first.

findings:
I annotated all 10 variants of ocflb-level-b-v1, which is 5 pairs with a DEFINER arm and an ADAPTER arm each (modulo 1 selects every variant). Metadata root: /Users/shawnli/Desktop/Honours/defects4j/supervisor_pipeline_runs/ocflb-level-b-v1. Design (FINAL_LEVEL_B_SPEC.md, PAIR_SELECTION.md): - Ownership is unique globally (production second caller of H2 plus a unit pin plus an isolated-repair proof) but ambiguous locally (neutral javadocs, omission or convention-mismatch faults). - Blinded gates V15/V16 confirm the local ambiguity: 60 graders, LOCAL_AMBIGUOUS for every pair (analysis/LOCAL_BLINDNESS.md). - Four pairs were revised after cue classes that exposed the fault were found: a bit-based range check in Lang-03; a contradicting adjacent term in Lang-04; a canonical 'raw & 0xff' at H2 in Compress-07; a unit-stating H3 javadoc in Math-05. What the reports concluded: 1. The pilot confirmed CASE C (PILOT_RESULTS.md, FINAL_EXPERIMENT_SUMMARY.md). - On the adversarial Chart pair, only a visible self-incriminating operator at the gold (V5) restored Sonnet (3/3). - A production second caller (V1), a sibling (V2) and explicit H2/H3 javadocs (V3/V4) all stayed at 0/3. V3 partly restored Opus (2/3). 2. Level B sits between Level A and Level C (results/FINAL_THESIS_INTERPRETATION.md, RESULT 1). - Adapter-arm Acc@1: Sonnet 0.64, Opus 0.545; Level A is 0.0/0.1 and Level C is 0.867/0.96. The definer arm is 0.76 for Sonnet and 0.733 for Opus. - Local specification controls attribution. Global evidence settles ownership but is not always retrieved or integrated. 3. Every failure is "gold discovered but misranked" (analysis/EVIDENCE_RETRIEVAL_ANALYSIS.md, results/FAILURE_TAXONOMY.md). - All answered runs opened the gold body. - Misses are concentrated on LB-CHART-01: 18 of 20 answered wrong runs. Sonnet scored 0/5 on both arms; Opus scored 1/5 (definer) and 0/5 (adapter). - The other misses are one Lang-04 adapter run (DEFINER_ATTRIBUTION) and one Compress-07 adapter run (FACADE_ATTRIBUTION, graded DEPTH_PRIOR). The Math and Compress no-answers are timeouts or budget exhaustion. 4. The failure is a convention prior, not a definer bias (FINAL_THESIS_INTERPRETATION.md section 3, analysis/MECHANISM_GRADING.md). - On Chart the agents assumed the offset points outward (point2 - point1) and convicted whichever hop disagreed. That is H2 in the adapter arm and H3 in the definer arm. - Graded mechanisms over the 20 misses: - LOCAL_ODDNESS plus EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE_NOT_RETRIEVED: 12/20. - EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE_MISREAD: 6/20. RingPlot.collapse was opened and explained away. - DEPTH_PRIOR: 1. - The pin testOffset was opened in 0 of 20 Chart runs. 5. Evidence retrieval helps but does not override a strong prior. - Sonnet Group E vs N Acc@1: 0.771 vs 0.533. Opus: 0.75 vs 0.5. - Retrieval rate by pair: Chart 4/10, Compress 10/10, Lang-03 9/10, Lang-04 4/10, Math 8/10. 6. Model differences (section 5). - Opus shows the same pattern with about 6x fewer tool calls and retrieves external evidence less often (0.36 vs 0.68 on the adapter arm). 7. Threat (section 7): the effect rests on a single pair, Chart. The reports recommend that v2 multiply the sign/direction family and move the external evidence off the chain files. My own observations (not stated in the reports), from reading the patches and manifests: - **Successes:** - Lang-03 (both arms) and the Math-05 adapter arm keep a visible extra operation at the gold ('* Byte.SIZE', '* top'), which is the V5-like cue, even though they passed V15/V16. - In Compress-07, Lang-03, Lang-04 and Math-05 the models' priors match the repository convention: - unsigned tar checksum; - 'in bits' in the facade javadoc; - String.regionMatches checking either case form; - the MINPACK enorm double division. - The decisive evidence is often close to the chain: - TarBuffer.digest sits next to H1 tally; - shortArrayToLong and scaledSumOfSquares are in the facade's file; - testScaledSumOfSquares and testShortArrayToLong share the trigger's test class. - **Chart** is the only pair where the natural prior contradicts the repository, so in both arms the correct hop looks wrong. The decisive second caller, RingPlot.collapse, uses the same '+ offset * percent' as the faulty nudge in the adapter arm, which invites the misreading seen in the MISREAD runs. - **Definer arms:** the pin and the second-caller test also fail (manifest all_empirically_failing_tests). That signal is available to agents but went unused on Chart. I counted search_depth_hops as call edges from the test method to the gold, including the ArcProbe.arc helper for Chart and StringUtils.equalsIgnoreCase for Lang-04.
